    Source grade — the badge next to a value shows its basis. Last changed next to a section title is the public version in which that section's content last changed, and links to Patch history.
    • Original (confirmed) A value taken directly from a row of the extracted original data with no signs of editing, or from the original client code
    • Estimated A value the restoration filled in because the original data has no field for it (e.g. rules that were server-only)
    • Changed from original (developer decision) A value that exists in the original but was set differently by developer decision
    • Unverified Values not yet backed by a source — shown in section titles — 2 on this page

    [Revived King] Tyrannosaurus: a fork creature cloned from the original Alpha Tyrannosaurus (2114) with Life, Attack, Accuracy, Defense, Evasion, Stun, Stagger resistance, difficulty and size raised ×1.3. The original Tyranno animations are applied to the zombie Tyranno model. One at Lv.15 in the center of the test island. It roars once each when combat starts and when Life first drops to 50% and 10% (screen shake, meteors), and at 10% Frenzy turns on (Attack ×1.5, attack delay ×0.85, animation ×1.15, until death). When Frenzy turns on it shakes off knockdown and stun, roars at once, takes no damage for 10s (“Blocked”), cannot be stunned or knocked down, and meanwhile regains Life up to 50% of max. Roar and Frenzy each happen only once. This species is not in the original.

    Fork
    Legacy data for the hostile creature with Ragdoll looks and animations. From 2026.09.28.1, ordinary Ragdolls are excluded from wild spawning and save restoration, and the companion is obtained through a separate one-time quest. It temporarily uses the original stat formulas and butchering rewards of the ordinary Sabertooth (2007). At Lv.15 and Unstable index 1: Life 1385.631, Attack 48.69, Defense 75. Walking, chasing, sleeping, stun and knockdown are linked with Kitty Punch ×5, Hind Kick Flurry ×3, Pounce, and a Pounce after a long wind-up, all using the shared damage check. The normal Pounce shortens its lunge to fit a nearby target and hits once on landing. The butt-wiggling wind-up Pounce makes the wiggle ×1.5 larger and the wind-up about ×1.5 longer. It leaps in a straight line in the initially aimed direction — 3.29 m for an ordinary Ragdoll, about 15.33 m for Macaron (70% of the previous version) — and does not stop near the target or track it mid-air. The wind-up version checks each target once along its flight path and stops moving at obstacles, water and map edges. Compared with the first test build, walk/chase speed is ×2 and body turn speed ×1.5. Kitty Punch strikes downward with the front paws 5 times. An attack cancelled during its telegraph does not count as used. If stun turns into knockdown, the previous idle ends and it switches to a looping limb-and-body flailing animation. After death it holds its final pose. The pet is offered through a separate “A New Companion” quest. Low stun / high knockback chances are follow-up work. The species existed in the original, but these are not the original's own attack values. Uses a dedicated mini portrait for sailing. 14 dedicated sound effects: three cries, purring, a hiss before attacking, a warning growl, real hit sounds, and knockdown, landing, footstep, swing and impact sounds. Follows the sound effect setting and player distance, and purrs while sleeping. Cries play one at a time per creature, and idling, hits or stun during combat are not mistaken for a new fight that repeats the cry. Footsteps and impact sounds are heard along with cries.

    Apex of the Ecosystem [Master] Macaron: a separate special creature, the approved Ragdoll scaled up ×4.66. Measured height about 5.98 m, matched to an ordinary Tarbosaurus. Only Life, Attack and Defense are ×1.5 the formulas of an ordinary Tarbo (2086) at the same level and Unstable index. Other stats and butchering rewards follow the ordinary Ragdoll, and stride, movement speed, collision and attack range are scaled up with its size. One is placed in the center of the elite test island. It uses the same Kitty Punch, Hind Kick Flurry and both kinds of Pounce as an ordinary Ragdoll, with landing checks scaled to its size. Uses a dedicated sailing portrait. Uses dedicated sound effects deeper than an ordinary Ragdoll's. Within 45 m its own BGM fades in, reaching the set maximum volume within 15 m. The regular background music lowers and returns when you move away or it dies. Loops a 78s section of the developer-chosen round-1 generated track, starting at 18s. Follows the background music setting.

    Fork
    Life, Attack and Defense apply 85% to the original formulas of an ordinary Tarbosaurus (2086) at the same level and instability. Other stats and the absolute regen per second keep the existing Gallimimus baseline (regen about 0.0596%/s of the new max Life). Existing creatures keep their remaining health ratio, death and part-break state. Therizinosaurus: fork model based on reference photos, 22 animations. Walk cycle 1.8s (120 cm/s); one-hand and two-hand attacks slowly gather power, then swing quickly through torso, arm and hand in order and follow through with recoil. The two-hand slam lifts one foot and leans back, then steps 80 cm forward and slams 4.3 m ahead in a 150° arc (damage 1–1.08s). The old charge was replaced by a 6-hit advancing slash series alternating left and right feet with the opposite arm. During the roughly 2.93s animation it moves 10.8 m straight ahead and slashes a 3.4 m radius, 130° arc in front at 0.53, 0.88, 1.23, 1.57, 1.92 and 2.27s. It keeps the initial aim direction and stops when blocked by obstacles, water or map edges. The spin ducks to the lower left, then turns 280° clockwise, with the damage window at 0.5–1.35s. Knockdown includes staggered reactions of limbs, neck and tail and a wobble after landing. Cries, charging, hit and knockdown sounds were tuned to a low, rough voice. 11 self-made sound effects are linked to all animations, following the sound effect setting and 7–45 m distance falloff from the player. The advancing slash hits each target once per slash; other attacks once per animation. All of these are fork values authored on developer request, not restored original values. Since 2026-09-24 it is no longer placed on the test island (the test island holds only the Revived King).
